fw-01: Say thank you politely in Korean. Use 감사하다 + -(스)ㅂ니다.
fw-02: Introduce yourself in one sentence (your name or job). Use 저 + topic particle 은/는.
fw-03: Ask what an object near the listener is. Use the demonstrative (그 + 거) with 뭐 + -예요?
fw-04: State the price of an item using a Sino-Korean number, the currency unit 원, and -이에요.
fw-05: Politely order a drink (e.g. coffee) with a counter. Use 주다 + -(으)세요.
fw-06: Ask where a location (e.g. station or restroom) is. Use 어디 + -예요?
fw-07: Tell someone that you speak a little Korean. Use the adverb 조금 with 한국어 and 하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
fw-08: Place an order for drinks at a cafe with quantity. Use 주다 + -(으)세요.
gr-01: Write one routine activity you do every day (e.g. studying or exercising). Use a 하다 verb in the polite present (-아요/어요).
gr-02: Write one sentence about an activity you completed yesterday. Use the time word 어제 and past tense -았/었어요.
gr-03: Say what you are doing right now. Use an action verb + -고 있어요.
gr-04: Say one thing you choose not to do or eat. Use the short negative adverb 안 with a polite present verb.
gr-05: State what beverage you drink. Use 마시다 in the polite present with object particle 을/를.
gr-06: Say where you study or work. Use a location noun with action location particle 에서 and a polite present verb.
gr-07: Compare two things or times (e.g. today and yesterday). Use the comparison particle 보다.
gr-08: Connect two contrasting statements into one sentence. Use an adjective or verb stem + -지만.
bg-04-01: State that you were the one who ordered the food. Use 저 + -가 (subject focus) and 주문하다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-04-02: Contrast one drink or food you like with one you do not. Use topic particle 은/는 for contrast and 좋아하다 + -지만.
bg-05-01: State that you are a student. Use 학생 + identification copula -이에요/예요.
bg-05-02: State that you are not a singer. Use 가수 + -이/가 and 아니다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-05-03: Point to an item and state that it is a desk. Use 이거는 with 책상 + -이에요/예요.
bg-05-04: Clarify that you are a student, not a teacher. Use 선생님 + -이/가 with 아니다 (-아요/어요), and 학생 + -이에요/예요.
bg-06-01: State that you have time today. Use 시간 + -이/가 and 있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-06-02: State that you eat a meal at a restaurant. Use 식당 + -에서 and 먹다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-06-03: Suggest meeting someone at three o'clock. Use the native Korean number for three + 시 + time particle -에, and 만나다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-06-04: State what object is in your room or bag. Use a location with static location particle -에 and 있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-01: State that you cook at home. Use 집 + action location particle -에서 and 요리하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-02: Suggest having lunch together with a friend. Use adverb 같이 with 점심 and 먹다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-03: Suggest taking a walk in the park together. Use 공원 + -에서 and 산책하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-04: A friend asks what you do this evening. Reply that you rest at home. Use 집 + -에서 and 쉬다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-01: State what you read every day. Use 책 + object particle -을/를 and 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-02: State that you like coffee (with contrast). Use 커피 + topic particle -은/는 for contrast and 좋아하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-03: Write a sentence stating that you learn Korean. Use 저 + topic particle -은/는, 한국어 + object particle -을/를, and 배우다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-04: State that you are eating pizza. Use 피자 + object particle -을/를 and 먹다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-01: State that you do not work on weekends. Use noun 일 with short negation 안 and 하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-02: State that you cannot swim due to inability. Use noun 수영 with negative adverb 못 and 하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-03: Explain that you cannot drink alcohol because you are driving. Use 운전하다 + -아/어서 with negative adverb 못 and 마시다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-04: State that this food is not expensive. Use short negation 안 with adjective 비싸다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-10-01: State where you went yesterday (e.g. library). Use time word 어제 and 가다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-10-02: State that you drank coffee a little while ago. Use time adverb 아까 and 마시다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-10-03: State that you wrote a diary entry in Korean. Use 한국어 + language particle -(으)로 and 쓰다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-10-04: State that you listened to music yesterday. Use time word 어제 and 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-11-01: Say what you are doing at the library right now. Use 도서관 + -에서 and 공부하다 + -고 있어요.
bg-11-02: State that you are resting at home right now. Use 집 + -에서 and 쉬다 + -고 있어요.
bg-11-03: State that you are wearing a hat. Use 모자 + object particle -을/를 and wear verb 쓰다 + -고 있어요.
bg-11-04: Reply to a friend that you are waiting for the bus. Use 버스 + object particle -을/를 and 기다리다 + -고 있어요.
bg-12-01: State that you wash your hands before eating a meal. Use 먹다 + -기 전에 and 손을 씻다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-12-02: State what you do when you are tired. Use 피곤하다 + -(으)ㄹ 때 and 쉬다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-12-03: State that it has been 3 months since you started learning Korean. Use 배우다 + -(으)ㄴ 지 and 되다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-12-04: State that you read a book before going to sleep. Use 자다 + -기 전에 and 책을 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-01: Connect two sequential actions: eating a meal and drinking coffee. Use 먹다 + -고 and 마시다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-13-02: Contrast the price and taste of a dish (expensive but delicious). Use 비싸다 + -지만 and 맛있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-03: Connect listening to music and reading a newspaper in the morning. Use 듣다 + -고 and 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-04: Contrast someone being busy with always being kind. Use 바쁘다 + -지만 and 친절하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-14-01: Write one sentence saying you rested at home because you were tired. Use 피곤하다 + -아/어서 and 쉬다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-14-02: Suggest going inside because it is cold outside. Use 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)니까 and 들어가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-14-03: Tell someone to close the window because it is cold outside. Use 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)니까 and 닫다 + -(으)세요.
bg-14-04: Politely apologize for being late to an appointment. Use 늦다 + -아/어서 and 죄송하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-15-01: State what improves if you read a lot of books. Use 읽다 + -(으)면 and 좋아지다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-15-02: State that you greet a friend while smiling. Use 웃다 + -(으)면서 and 인사하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-15-03: State that you drink coffee or tea in the morning. Use 마시다 + -거나 to connect the alternatives.
bg-15-04: State two alternate activities you do if you have free time. Use 있다 + -(으)면 and 읽다 + -거나.
bg-16-01: Set the background that you are going to the bookstore now. Use 서점 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -는데.
bg-16-02: Suggest going for a walk because the weather is nice. Use 좋다 + -(으)ㄴ데 and 산책하다 + -(으)ㄹ까요?
bg-16-03: Politely decline an invitation by saying you want to go but are busy today. Use -고 싶다 + -(으)ㄴ데 and 바쁘다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-16-04: Politely preface a question by saying you have a question. Use 질문 + -이/가 and 있다 + -는데.
bg-17-01: Tell someone to read a book slowly. Use adverb 천천히 and 읽다 + -(으)세요.
bg-17-02: Politely ask someone to speak slowly for you. Use adverb 천천히 and 말하다 + -아/어 주세요.
bg-17-03: Ask someone to listen to your story as a favor. Use 이야기 + object particle -을/를 and 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + -아/어 주세요.
bg-17-04: Ask someone to close the door for you because it is noisy outside. Use 닫다 + -아/어 주세요.
bg-18-01: Ask for permission to eat an apple. Use 사과 + object particle -을/를 and 먹다 + -아/어도 돼요?
bg-18-02: State that you must clean your room today. Use 방 + object particle -을/를 and 청소하다 + -아/어야 돼요.
bg-18-03: State that you may go home now because work or class is finished. Use 집 + -에 and 가다 + -아/어도 돼요.
bg-18-04: Ask if you may charge your phone here. Use 휴대폰 + object particle -을/를 and 충전하다 + -아/어도 돼요?
bg-19-01: Tell someone not to drink coffee at night. Use 커피 + object particle -을/를 and 마시다 + -지 마세요.
bg-19-02: Tell someone not to enter because it is dangerous. Use 위험하다 + -(으)니까 and 들어가다 + -지 마세요.
bg-19-03: Reassure a friend not to worry too much. Use 걱정하다 + -지 마세요.
bg-19-04: Encourage someone not to give up until the end. Use 끝까지 and 포기하다 + -지 마세요.
bg-20-01: State that you can play the piano. Use 피아노 + object particle -을/를 and instrument verb 치다 + -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요.
bg-20-02: Explain that you cannot meet today because you are busy. Use 바쁘다 + -아/어서 and 만나다 + -(으)ㄹ 수 없어요.
bg-20-03: State that you can listen to Korean songs. Use 한국 노래 with 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요.
bg-20-04: State that you cannot drive due to lack of skill. Use 운전 + object particle -을/를 and 못하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-21-01: Suggest drinking coffee together. Use adverb 같이 and 마시다 + -(으)ㄹ까요?
bg-21-02: Promise to call someone tomorrow. Use time word 내일 and 전화하다 + -(으)ㄹ게요.
bg-21-03: Express your personal intention to rest at home today. Use 집 + -에서 and 쉬다 + -(으)ㄹ래요.
bg-21-04: Volunteer to buy dinner for your friend. Use 저 + -가 (subject focus) and 사다 + -(으)ㄹ게요.
bg-22-01: Ask a friend if they have tried eating kimchi. Use 김치 and 먹다 + -아/어 봤어요?
bg-22-02: State that you have never been skiing (riding skis). Use 스키 with 타다 + -(으)ㄴ 적이 없어요.
bg-22-03: State that you have watched Korean dramas before. Use 한국 드라마 with 보다 + -(으)ㄴ 적이 있어요.
bg-22-04: Recommend visiting Jeju Island to a friend. Use 제주도 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -아/어 보세요.
bg-23-01: State that you go to the library to study. Use 공부하다 + -(으)러 and 가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-23-02: State that you intend to buy a computer. Use 컴퓨터 and 사다 + -(으)려고 해요.
bg-23-03: State that you decided to meet someone at 2 o'clock. Use 2시 + time particle -에 and 만나다 + -기로 했어요.
bg-23-04: State that you decided to go to Korea. Use 한국 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -기로 했어요.
